title: Python Programming Mastery
subtitle: Complete Guide from Beginner to Advanced
author: Programming Experts

pages.title: What is Python?
pages.content: Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its simplicity and readability. It was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. Python is widely used in web development, data science, artificial intelligence, automation, and software development. Its simple syntax makes it one of the best programming languages for beginners.
keyPoints: Used in AI, web, and automation

quiz.question: Who created Python?
quiz.explanation: Python was created by Guido van Rossum in 1991.

pages.title: Why Learn Python?
pages.content: Python is one of the most popular programming languages due to its simplicity and versatility. It supports multiple programming paradigms such as object-oriented, procedural, and functional programming. Python is widely used in modern industries including machine learning, web development, data analysis, and automation.
keyPoints: Used in data science and AI

quiz.question: Which field commonly uses Python?
quiz.explanation: Python is widely used in data science, AI, and web development.

pages.title: Installing Python
pages.content: Python can be installed from the official website python.org. After downloading the installer, follow the installation steps and make sure to check the option 'Add Python to PATH'. Once installed, you can run Python programs using the command prompt or terminal.
keyPoints: Add Python to PATH during installation

quiz.question: Which command checks Python version?
quiz.explanation: python --version displays the installed Python version.

pages.title: Running Python Programs
pages.content: Python programs can be executed using the Python interpreter. You can run Python code in three main ways: using the interactive Python shell, running Python files (.py) from the terminal, or using an Integrated Development Environment (IDE).

quiz.question: What is the extension of Python files?
quiz.explanation: Python files use the .py extension.

pages.title: Python IDEs
pages.content: Python code can be written using various editors and IDEs. Popular Python IDEs include Visual Studio Code, PyCharm, and Jupyter Notebook. These tools provide features like syntax highlighting, debugging tools, and code completion which help developers write better code.
pages.exampleCode:
# Example Python code in any IDE
print('Learning Python with Eklav')
keyPoints: VS Code is lightweight and popular
PyCharm is a powerful Python IDE
Jupyter Notebook is used in data science

quiz.question: Which IDE is commonly used for Python development?
quiz.explanation: VS Code, PyCharm, and Jupyter Notebook are popular Python development tools.

chapters.title: Variables and Data Types
chapters.description: Understanding how Python stores and manages different types of data

pages.title: What are Variables?
pages.content: Variables are used to store data values in a program. In Python, variables are created when you assign a value to them. Python automatically determines the data type based on the assigned value.
keyPoints: No need to declare variable type

quiz.question: How are variables created in Python?
quiz.explanation: In Python, variables are created when a value is assigned.

pages.title: Variable Naming Rules
pages.content: Variable names must follow certain rules. A variable name must start with a letter or underscore, cannot start with a number, and cannot be a Python keyword.
keyPoints: Must start with letter or underscore

quiz.question: Which of the following is a valid variable name?
quiz.explanation: _name is valid because it starts with an underscore.

pages.title: Multiple Variable Assignment
pages.content: Python allows assigning values to multiple variables in a single line. You can also assign the same value to multiple variables at once.
pages.exampleCode:
x, y, z = 10, 20, 30
print(x, y, z)

a = b = c = 5
print(a, b, c)
keyPoints: Multiple variables can be assigned in one line
Same value can be assigned to multiple variables

quiz.question: Which syntax assigns the same value to multiple variables?
quiz.explanation: a = b = c = 5 assigns the same value to all variables.

pages.title: Basic Data Types
pages.content: Python supports multiple built-in data types including integers, floats, strings, and booleans. These data types define the kind of data stored in variables.

quiz.question: Which data type represents text?
quiz.explanation: Strings (str) represent text data.

pages.title: Checking Data Types
pages.content: Python provides the type() function to check the data type of a variable. This helps developers understand what type of data a variable contains.

quiz.question: Which function checks the data type of a variable?
quiz.explanation: type() returns the data type of a variable.

pages.title: Type Conversion
pages.content: Type conversion allows changing one data type into another. Python provides built-in functions such as int(), float(), and str() for converting data types.

quiz.question: Which function converts a value to integer?
quiz.explanation: int() converts a value into an integer.

chapters.title: Python Operators
chapters.description: Understanding different types of operators used in Python programs

pages.title: Introduction to Operators
pages.content: Operators are special symbols used to perform operations on variables and values. Python provides several types of operators such as arithmetic, comparison, logical, assignment, membership, and identity operators.
keyPoints: Python has multiple types of operators
Operators work with variables and data

quiz.question: What are operators used for?
quiz.explanation: Operators perform operations such as addition, comparison, and logical evaluation.

pages.title: Arithmetic Operators
pages.content: Arithmetic operators are used to perform mathematical calculations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
pages.exampleCode:
a = 10
b = 3

print(a + b)
print(a - b)
print(a * b)
print(a / b)

quiz.question: Which operator is used for multiplication?
quiz.explanation: * is the multiplication operator.

pages.title: Comparison Operators
pages.content: Comparison operators compare two values and return either True or False depending on the result of the comparison.
pages.exampleCode:
a = 10
b = 5

print(a > b)
print(a < b)
print(a == b)

quiz.question: Which operator checks if two values are equal?
quiz.explanation: == is used to compare two values for equality.

pages.title: Logical Operators
pages.content: Logical operators are used to combine conditional statements. Python provides three logical operators: and, or, and not.
pages.exampleCode:
age = 20
hasID = True

print(age > 18 and hasID)
keyPoints: and returns True if both conditions are True
or returns True if one condition is True

quiz.question: Which logical operator returns True when both conditions are True?
quiz.explanation: The 'and' operator returns True only if both conditions are True.

pages.title: Assignment Operators
pages.content: Assignment operators are used to assign values to variables. Python also supports shorthand assignment operators that combine operations with assignment.

quiz.question: What does the += operator do?
quiz.explanation: += adds a value to the variable and assigns the result.

pages.title: Membership and Identity Operators
pages.content: Membership operators check if a value exists in a sequence like a list or string. Identity operators compare the memory location of two objects.
pages.exampleCode:
numbers = [1,2,3,4]

print(2 in numbers)

x = 10
y = 10
print(x is y)
keyPoints: not in checks if value does not exist
is not checks if objects are different

quiz.question: Which operator checks if a value exists in a list?
quiz.explanation: The 'in' operator checks membership in a sequence.

chapters.title: Conditional Statements
chapters.description: Making decisions in Python programs using if, elif, and else

pages.title: Introduction to Conditional Statements
pages.content: Conditional statements allow a program to make decisions based on conditions. Python uses if, elif, and else statements to execute different blocks of code depending on whether a condition is True or False.
keyPoints: Python uses if, elif, and else

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to check a condition in Python?
quiz.explanation: The 'if' statement is used to check a condition in Python.

pages.title: The if Statement
pages.content: The if statement is used to test a condition. If the condition is True, the code block inside the if statement is executed.
keyPoints: Runs code only if condition is True

quiz.question: What happens if the if condition is False?
quiz.explanation: If the condition is False, the code block inside the if statement is skipped.

pages.title: The if-else Statement
pages.content: The else statement runs when the condition in the if statement is False. It provides an alternative block of code.
keyPoints: else runs when if condition is False

quiz.question: When does the else block run?
quiz.explanation: The else block executes when the if condition evaluates to False.

pages.title: The if-elif-else Statement
pages.content: The elif statement allows checking multiple conditions. It stands for 'else if'. Python evaluates conditions in order and executes the first True block.

quiz.question: What does 'elif' stand for?
quiz.explanation: 'elif' means 'else if' in Python.

pages.title: Nested Conditional Statements
pages.content: Nested conditions occur when an if statement is placed inside another if statement. This helps check complex decision logic.
keyPoints: Nested conditions place if inside another if

quiz.question: What is a nested if statement?
options: Two if statements in different files
quiz.explanation: Nested if means placing one if statement inside another.

pages.title: Short-Hand if Statement
pages.content: Python allows writing simple if statements in a single line. This is called shorthand if or conditional expression.
pages.exampleCode:
age = 18
print('Adult') if age >= 18 else print('Minor')

quiz.question: What is another name for short-hand if?
quiz.explanation: Short-hand if is also known as a ternary expression.

chapters.title: Loops
chapters.description: Repeating tasks in Python using loops such as for and while

pages.title: Introduction to Loops
pages.content: Loops allow programmers to repeat a block of code multiple times without writing it repeatedly. Python mainly provides two types of loops: for loop and while loop. Loops are useful when working with lists, ranges, and repetitive tasks.
pages.exampleCode:
for i in range(3):
    print('Hello Python')
keyPoints: Python has two main loops: for and while
Commonly used with lists and ranges

quiz.question: What is the purpose of loops?
options: To repeat a block of code
quiz.explanation: Loops are used to repeat a block of code multiple times.

pages.title: The for Loop
pages.content: The for loop is used to iterate over a sequence such as a list, tuple, string, or range. It executes the block of code once for each item in the sequence.

quiz.question: Which function is commonly used with for loops?
quiz.explanation: range() is commonly used with for loops to generate sequences.

pages.title: The while Loop
pages.content: The while loop executes a block of code as long as a condition remains True. It is useful when the number of iterations is not known beforehand.
keyPoints: Used when number of iterations is unknown
Condition is checked before each loop

quiz.question: When does a while loop stop?
quiz.explanation: The while loop stops when the condition becomes False.

pages.title: The break Statement
pages.content: The break statement is used to immediately exit a loop even if the loop condition is still True. It is commonly used when a specific condition is met.
keyPoints: Used when a condition is met
Works with both for and while loops

quiz.question: What does the break statement do?
quiz.explanation: break stops the loop immediately.

pages.title: The continue Statement
pages.content: The continue statement skips the current iteration of the loop and moves to the next iteration without stopping the loop completely.

quiz.question: What does continue do in a loop?
quiz.explanation: continue skips the current iteration and moves to the next.

pages.title: Nested Loops
pages.content: A nested loop is a loop inside another loop. Nested loops are commonly used when working with matrices, tables, or complex iterations.
keyPoints: Inner loop runs for each outer iteration

quiz.question: What is a nested loop?
quiz.explanation: Nested loop means placing one loop inside another.

chapters.title: Python Strings
chapters.description: Working with text data using Python strings

pages.title: Introduction to Strings
pages.content: A string in Python is a sequence of characters used to store text. Strings can be created using single quotes (' '), double quotes (" "), or triple quotes for multi-line text.
pages.exampleCode:
name = 'Python'
message = "Welcome to Python"
print(name)
print(message)
keyPoints: Created using single or double quotes
Commonly used for messages and user input

quiz.question: What is a string in Python?
quiz.explanation: A string is a sequence of characters used to represent text.

pages.title: String Indexing
pages.content: String indexing allows accessing individual characters of a string using their position. Indexes start from 0 in Python.

quiz.question: What is the index of the first character in a string?
quiz.explanation: Python indexing starts at 0.

pages.title: String Slicing
pages.content: String slicing allows extracting a portion of a string using start and end indexes. The syntax is string[start:end].

quiz.question: What does text[0:3] return?
quiz.explanation: Slicing from index 0 to 3 returns the first three characters.

pages.title: String Methods
pages.content: Python provides many built-in methods to manipulate strings such as lower(), upper(), strip(), and replace(). These methods help modify or analyze string content.

quiz.question: Which method converts a string to uppercase?
quiz.explanation: upper() converts all characters to uppercase.

pages.title: String Concatenation
pages.content: String concatenation means joining two or more strings together. This is usually done using the + operator.
pages.exampleCode:
first = 'Hello'
second = 'Python'
message = first + ' ' + second
print(message)

quiz.question: Which operator is used for string concatenation?
quiz.explanation: + is used to join strings together.

pages.title: String Formatting
pages.content: String formatting allows inserting variables into strings. Python supports several formatting techniques including f-strings, format(), and % formatting.
pages.exampleCode:
name = 'John'
age = 25
print(f'My name is {name} and I am {age} years old')

quiz.question: Which method is commonly used for modern string formatting?
quiz.explanation: f-strings are the modern and recommended way for formatting strings.

chapters.title: Python Lists
chapters.description: Understanding lists and how to store multiple values in Python

pages.title: Introduction to Lists
pages.content: A list in Python is a collection used to store multiple values in a single variable. Lists are ordered, changeable (mutable), and allow duplicate values. Lists are created using square brackets [].

quiz.question: Which symbol is used to create a list in Python?
quiz.explanation: Lists are created using square brackets [].

pages.title: Accessing List Elements
pages.content: List elements can be accessed using indexes. Indexes start from 0, meaning the first element has index 0.

quiz.question: What is the index of the first element in a list?
quiz.explanation: The first element of a list has index 0.

pages.title: List Slicing
pages.content: List slicing allows extracting a portion of a list using start and end indexes. The syntax is list[start:end].
keyPoints: Extract a portion of a list

quiz.question: What does numbers[1:3] return?
quiz.explanation: numbers[1:3] returns elements at index 1 and 2.

pages.title: Adding Elements to Lists
pages.content: Python provides several methods to add elements to lists such as append(), insert(), and extend().
keyPoints: insert() adds element at specific position

quiz.question: Which method adds an element to the end of a list?
quiz.explanation: append() adds an element to the end of a list.

pages.title: Removing Elements from Lists
pages.content: Python lists allow removing elements using methods such as remove(), pop(), and clear().

quiz.question: Which method removes an element by index?
quiz.explanation: pop() removes element using its index.

pages.title: List Comprehension
pages.content: List comprehension provides a short and efficient way to create lists using a single line of code.
pages.exampleCode:
numbers = [x for x in range(5)]
print(numbers)

quiz.question: What is list comprehension used for?
options: Creating lists in a compact way
quiz.explanation: List comprehension is used to create lists in a concise way.

chapters.title: Tuples and Sets
chapters.description: Understanding tuples and sets for storing collections of data in Python

pages.title: Introduction to Tuples
pages.content: A tuple is a collection used to store multiple items in a single variable. Tuples are ordered and immutable, meaning their values cannot be changed after creation.

quiz.question: Which symbol is used to create a tuple?
quiz.explanation: Tuples are created using parentheses ().

pages.title: Accessing Tuple Elements
pages.content: Tuple elements can be accessed using indexes similar to lists. Indexing starts from 0, and negative indexing can also be used to access elements from the end.

quiz.question: What does colors[-1] return?
quiz.explanation: Negative indexing accesses elements from the end.

pages.title: Tuple Methods
pages.content: Tuples have limited built-in methods compared to lists. The most commonly used methods are count() and index().
keyPoints: count() counts occurrences of a value
Tuples have fewer methods because they are immutable

quiz.question: Which method counts occurrences of a value in a tuple?
quiz.explanation: count() returns the number of occurrences of a value.

pages.title: Introduction to Sets
pages.content: A set is an unordered collection of unique elements. Sets are useful for removing duplicates and performing mathematical operations like union and intersection.

quiz.question: Which feature is unique to sets?
quiz.explanation: Sets automatically remove duplicate values.

pages.title: Set Methods
pages.content: Python provides methods such as add(), remove(), and clear() to modify sets.

quiz.question: Which method adds an element to a set?
quiz.explanation: add() is used to insert elements into a set.

pages.title: Set Operations
pages.content: Sets support mathematical operations such as union, intersection, and difference. These operations help compare elements between sets.

quiz.question: Which method finds common elements between sets?
quiz.explanation: intersection() returns common elements between sets.

chapters.title: Python Dictionaries
chapters.description: Understanding dictionaries for storing key-value pairs in Python

pages.title: Introduction to Dictionaries
pages.content: A dictionary in Python is a collection used to store data in key-value pairs. Dictionaries are ordered, changeable (mutable), and do not allow duplicate keys.

quiz.question: What does a dictionary store?
quiz.explanation: Dictionaries store data using key-value pairs.

pages.title: Accessing Dictionary Values
pages.content: Dictionary values can be accessed using their keys. This allows retrieving specific values stored in the dictionary.

quiz.question: How do you access a value in a dictionary?
quiz.explanation: Dictionary values are accessed using their keys.

pages.title: Adding and Updating Values
pages.content: New key-value pairs can be added to a dictionary, and existing values can be updated using assignment.
keyPoints: New keys can be added easily

quiz.question: What happens if you assign a value to an existing key?
quiz.explanation: Assigning a value to an existing key updates its value.

pages.title: Dictionary Methods
pages.content: Python provides several built-in methods to work with dictionaries such as keys(), values(), and items().

quiz.question: Which method returns all dictionary keys?
quiz.explanation: keys() returns all the keys in the dictionary.

pages.title: Removing Dictionary Items
pages.content: Dictionary items can be removed using methods like pop(), popitem(), and clear().

quiz.question: Which method removes a specific key from a dictionary?
quiz.explanation: pop() removes the specified key from the dictionary.

pages.title: Iterating Dictionaries
pages.content: You can loop through dictionaries using for loops to access keys, values, or both.

quiz.question: Which method returns key-value pairs for iteration?
quiz.explanation: items() returns key-value pairs for iteration.

chapters.title: Python Functions
chapters.description: Understanding how to create and use functions in Python

pages.title: Introduction to Functions
pages.content: A function is a block of reusable code that performs a specific task. Functions help make programs modular, readable, and easier to maintain.

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
quiz.explanation: Functions in Python are defined using the def keyword.

pages.title: Calling a Function
pages.content: Once a function is defined, it can be executed by calling its name followed by parentheses.
keyPoints: Functions must be called to execute
Function can be called multiple times

quiz.question: How do you execute a function?
quiz.explanation: Functions run when their name is called with parentheses.

pages.title: Function Parameters
pages.content: Parameters allow passing data into functions. This makes functions more flexible and reusable.

quiz.question: What are values passed into a function called?
quiz.explanation: Values passed into a function are called arguments.

pages.title: Return Statement
pages.content: The return statement sends a value back from a function. This allows functions to produce results that can be used elsewhere in the program.
pages.exampleCode:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(3, 5)
print(result)
keyPoints: Returned value can be stored in a variable

quiz.question: What does the return statement do?
options: Returns a value from the function
quiz.explanation: return sends a result back from a function.

pages.title: Default Parameters
pages.content: Default parameters allow assigning default values to function parameters. If no argument is passed, the default value is used.
pages.exampleCode:
def greet(name='Student'):
    print('Hello', name)

greet()
greet('Alice')

quiz.question: What happens if no argument is passed to a default parameter?
quiz.explanation: The default value is used if no argument is provided.

pages.title: Lambda Functions
pages.content: A lambda function is a small anonymous function defined using the lambda keyword. It is often used for simple operations in a single line.
pages.exampleCode:
add = lambda a, b: a + b
print(add(4, 6))

quiz.question: Which keyword defines a lambda function?
quiz.explanation: Lambda functions are defined using the lambda keyword.

chapters.title: Modules and Packages
chapters.description: Organizing and reusing Python code using modules and packages

pages.title: Introduction to Modules
pages.content: A module is a file containing Python code such as variables, functions, and classes. Modules help organize code and allow developers to reuse functionality across different programs.
pages.exampleCode:
# example module usage
import math

print(math.sqrt(16))
keyPoints: Can include functions, variables, and classes

quiz.question: What is a module in Python?
quiz.explanation: A module is a Python file that contains functions, variables, or classes.

pages.title: Importing Modules
pages.content: Python provides the import keyword to use modules. Once a module is imported, its functions and variables can be used in the program.
keyPoints: Access module functions using dot notation

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to include a module?
quiz.explanation: The import keyword is used to include modules in Python.

pages.title: Importing Specific Functions
pages.content: Instead of importing the entire module, Python allows importing specific functions using the from keyword.

quiz.question: Which syntax imports only a specific function?
quiz.explanation: from module import function imports a specific function.

pages.title: Creating Custom Modules
pages.content: Developers can create their own modules by writing Python code in a file and importing it into another program.
pages.exampleCode:
# file: mymodule.py

def greet(name):
    return 'Hello ' + name

# main file
import mymodule
print(mymodule.greet('John'))
keyPoints: Import custom modules like built-in modules

quiz.question: What file extension is used for Python modules?
quiz.explanation: Python modules are saved with the .py extension.

pages.title: Introduction to Packages
pages.content: A package is a collection of multiple modules organized into directories. Packages help structure large Python projects.
pages.exampleCode:
# Example package structure
mypackage/
   module1.py
   module2.py

quiz.question: What is a package in Python?
quiz.explanation: A package is a collection of modules organized in a directory.

pages.title: Using pip and External Packages
pages.content: Python provides pip, a package manager used to install external libraries and packages from the Python Package Index (PyPI).

quiz.question: Which tool installs external Python packages?
quiz.explanation: pip is the Python package manager used to install libraries.

chapters.title: File Handling
chapters.description: Reading, writing, and managing files using Python

pages.title: Introduction to File Handling
pages.content: File handling allows Python programs to read data from files and write data to files. This is useful for storing data permanently outside the program.
keyPoints: Python can read and write files
Files must be opened before use
Files should be closed after use

quiz.question: What is the purpose of file handling?
quiz.explanation: File handling is used to store and retrieve data from files.

pages.title: Opening Files
pages.content: Python uses the open() function to open files. The open() function requires the file name and mode such as read, write, or append.
keyPoints: open() is used to open files
Common modes include read, write, append

quiz.question: Which function is used to open a file in Python?
quiz.explanation: The open() function is used to open files.

pages.title: File Modes
pages.content: File modes define how a file should be opened. Common modes include 'r' for reading, 'w' for writing, and 'a' for appending.
pages.exampleCode:
# read mode
open('file.txt', 'r')

# write mode
open('file.txt', 'w')

quiz.question: Which mode opens a file for writing?
quiz.explanation: The 'w' mode opens a file for writing.

pages.title: Reading Files
pages.content: Python provides methods such as read(), readline(), and readlines() to read file content.
keyPoints: readlines() reads all lines as list

quiz.question: Which method reads one line from a file?
quiz.explanation: readline() reads a single line from the file.

pages.title: Writing Files
pages.content: Python can write data to files using the write() method. If the file does not exist, Python will create it in write mode.

quiz.question: Which method writes data to a file?
quiz.explanation: write() is used to insert text into a file.

pages.title: Using the with Statement
pages.content: The with statement automatically handles opening and closing files. This makes the code safer and easier to manage.
keyPoints: Recommended way to work with files

quiz.question: Why is the with statement recommended?
quiz.explanation: The with statement automatically closes the file after use.

chapters.title: Exception Handling
chapters.description: Handling errors and exceptions in Python programs

pages.title: Introduction to Exceptions
pages.content: Exceptions are errors that occur during the execution of a program. Python provides a way to handle these errors using exception handling so the program does not crash unexpectedly.

quiz.question: What is an exception?
quiz.explanation: An exception is an error that occurs during program execution.

pages.title: The try and except Block
pages.content: The try block allows testing code for errors, while the except block handles the error if it occurs.

quiz.question: Which block handles errors in Python?
quiz.explanation: The except block handles errors when they occur.

pages.title: Handling Specific Exceptions
pages.content: Python allows handling specific types of exceptions such as ZeroDivisionError, ValueError, or TypeError.
keyPoints: Common errors include ValueError and TypeError

quiz.question: Which error occurs when converting invalid text to integer?
quiz.explanation: ValueError occurs when a value is inappropriate for the operation.

pages.title: The else Block
pages.content: The else block runs if no exceptions occur in the try block. It allows separating normal code from error handling.

quiz.question: When does the else block run?
quiz.explanation: The else block executes only if no exception occurs.

pages.title: The finally Block
pages.content: The finally block always executes regardless of whether an exception occurs or not. It is often used for cleanup operations like closing files.

quiz.question: Which block always executes?
quiz.explanation: The finally block always runs regardless of exceptions.

pages.title: Raising Exceptions
pages.content: Python allows developers to raise exceptions manually using the raise keyword. This helps enforce rules in programs.

quiz.question: Which keyword raises an exception manually?
quiz.explanation: The raise keyword is used to generate exceptions manually.

chapters.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
chapters.description: Understanding classes, objects, and OOP concepts in Python

pages.title: Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming
pages.content: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm that organizes code using objects and classes. It helps structure large programs and promotes code reusability.

quiz.question: What does OOP stand for?
quiz.explanation: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming.

pages.title: Classes and Objects
pages.content: A class is a blueprint for creating objects. An object is an instance of a class that contains data and methods.
pages.exampleCode:
class Person:
    name = 'John'

p = Person()
print(p.name)
keyPoints: Object is an instance of a class

quiz.question: What is an object?
quiz.explanation: An object is an instance created from a class.

pages.title: Constructors
pages.content: Constructors are special methods used to initialize objects when they are created. In Python, the constructor is defined using the __init__ method.
keyPoints: Automatically runs when object is created

quiz.question: Which method acts as a constructor in Python?
quiz.explanation: __init__ is the constructor method in Python.

pages.title: Inheritance
pages.content: Inheritance allows one class to inherit properties and methods from another class. This promotes code reuse and hierarchical relationships.
keyPoints: Child class inherits from parent class

quiz.question: What is inheritance used for?
quiz.explanation: Inheritance allows code reuse between classes.

pages.title: Encapsulation
pages.content: Encapsulation restricts direct access to certain variables and methods. It helps protect data and improves program security.

quiz.question: How are private variables defined in Python?
quiz.explanation: Private variables are defined using double underscore (__).

pages.title: Polymorphism
pages.content: Polymorphism allows methods to behave differently depending on the object calling them. This helps write flexible and reusable code.
keyPoints: Same method name with different behavior

quiz.question: What is polymorphism?
quiz.explanation: Polymorphism allows methods to behave differently for different objects.

chapters.title: Python Mini Projects
chapters.description: Applying Python concepts by building simple real-world projects

pages.title: Calculator Project
pages.content: This project builds a simple calculator that performs addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. It helps practice variables, functions, and user input.
pages.exampleCode:
num1 = int(input('Enter first number: '))
num2 = int(input('Enter second number: '))

print('Addition:', num1 + num2)
print('Subtraction:', num1 - num2)
print('Multiplication:', num1 * num2)
print('Division:', num1 / num2)

quiz.question: Which function takes input from the user?
quiz.explanation: input() is used to take user input in Python.

pages.title: Number Guessing Game
pages.content: In this game, the computer randomly selects a number, and the user tries to guess it. The program provides hints if the guess is too high or too low.
pages.exampleCode:
import random

number = random.randint(1,10)
guess = int(input('Guess the number: '))

if guess == number:
    print('Correct!')
else:
    print('Wrong! The number was', number)

quiz.question: Which module generates random numbers?
quiz.explanation: The random module generates random numbers.

pages.title: To-Do List Application
pages.content: This project creates a simple to-do list where users can add tasks and view them. It helps practice lists and loops.
pages.exampleCode:
tasks = []

while True:
    task = input('Enter task (or quit): ')
    if task == 'quit':
        break
    tasks.append(task)

print('Your Tasks:', tasks)

quiz.question: Which data structure is used to store tasks?
quiz.explanation: Lists are used to store multiple tasks.

pages.title: Password Generator
pages.content: This project generates random passwords using letters, numbers, and symbols. It demonstrates working with strings and randomization.
pages.exampleCode:
import random
import string

characters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
password = ''.join(random.choice(characters) for i in range(8))
print('Generated Password:', password)

quiz.question: Which module provides letters and digits for password generation?
quiz.explanation: The string module provides character sets.

pages.title: Simple File Organizer
pages.content: This project organizes files in a directory by moving them into folders based on their file type.

quiz.question: Which module is used to interact with the operating system?
quiz.explanation: The os module is used to interact with the operating system.

pages.title: Fetching Data from an API
pages.content: This project fetches data from an external API using Python. It introduces working with web data and external services.

quiz.question: Which library is commonly used to fetch API data in Python?
quiz.explanation: The requests library is widely used for API requests.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its readability and simplicity.

interviewQuestions.question: Who created Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and released in 1991.

interviewQuestions.question: What are the key features of Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: Python features include simplicity, readability, dynamic typing, large libraries, and cross-platform compatibility.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a variable in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: A variable is a container used to store data values in a program.

interviewQuestions.question: What are Python data types?
interviewQuestions.answer: Common Python data types include int, float, string, boolean, list, tuple, set, and dictionary.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between a list and a tuple?
interviewQuestions.answer: Lists are mutable (can change), while tuples are immutable (cannot change after creation).

interviewQuestions.question: What is a dictionary in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: A dictionary is a collection of key-value pairs used to store structured data.

interviewQuestions.question: What are Python operators?
interviewQuestions.answer: Operators are symbols used to perform operations on variables and values such as arithmetic, comparison, and logical operations.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between == and = in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: = assigns a value to a variable, while == compares two values for equality.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a loop in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: A loop allows executing a block of code multiple times using constructs like for and while.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a function in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: A function is a reusable block of code designed to perform a specific task.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the return statement?
interviewQuestions.answer: The return statement sends a value back from a function to the caller.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a module in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: A module is a file containing Python code such as functions, variables, and classes.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a package in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: A package is a collection of modules organized in directories.

interviewQuestions.question: What is file handling in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: File handling allows programs to read from and write to files stored on the system.

interviewQuestions.question: What is exception handling?
interviewQuestions.answer: Exception handling is a mechanism to manage runtime errors using try, except, and finally blocks.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between syntax errors and exceptions?
interviewQuestions.answer: Syntax errors occur when code violates Python grammar rules, while exceptions occur during program execution.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Object-Oriented Programming?
interviewQuestions.answer: OOP is a programming paradigm based on objects and classes that organize code into reusable components.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a class in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: A class is a blueprint for creating objects that contain properties and methods.

interviewQuestions.question: What is an object in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: An object is an instance of a class containing data and behavior.

interviewQuestions.question: What is inheritance in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: Inheritance allows a class to inherit properties and methods from another class.

interviewQuestions.question: What is polymorphism?
interviewQuestions.answer: Polymorphism allows methods to behave differently depending on the object that calls them.

interviewQuestions.question: What is encapsulation?
interviewQuestions.answer: Encapsulation restricts direct access to data and protects it using private variables.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a lambda function?
interviewQuestions.answer: A lambda function is a small anonymous function defined using the lambda keyword.

interviewQuestions.question: What are Python decorators?
interviewQuestions.answer: Decorators are functions that modify the behavior of other functions without changing their code.

interviewQuestions.question: What are generators in Python?
interviewQuestions.answer: Generators are functions that return an iterator using the yield keyword.

interviewQuestions.question: What is list comprehension?
interviewQuestions.answer: List comprehension provides a concise way to create lists using a single line of code.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between deep copy and shallow copy?
interviewQuestions.answer: A shallow copy duplicates references, while a deep copy duplicates the actual objects recursively.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL)?
interviewQuestions.answer: The GIL ensures that only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time in CPython.

interviewQuestions.question: What is pip?
interviewQuestions.answer: pip is the Python package manager used to install external libraries from PyPI.
